title: The Bright Moon and Me
program_note:
Written for the Elite Trio of Kaohsiung, Taiwan, The Bright Moon and Me is a 5:45-6:00 composition, loosely inspired by the Wang Wei (Tang Dynasty) poem In the House of Bamboo (竹 里 館):

獨 坐 幽 篁 裡                Sitting alone, in the secluded bamboo grove,

彈 琴 復 長 嘯                I pluck the qin*, my calls long echoing.

深 林 人 不 知                In the deep woods, others do not perceive

明 月 來 相 照                The bright moon and me upon each other glowing.

* Qin, or guqin, is a seven-string Chinese Zither.

(Translation by David S. Lefkowitz)

Although there are some specific relationships between the poem and the music — musical echoes, certain sounds reminiscent of the qin, references to the moon — on the whole the music exists on its own, not following the form or the content of the poem.  At the end of the composition, however, the performers are asked to speak the words of the poem.  This can be done in either Chinese or English, and should more-or-less follow the speech-rhythms shown in the music.  These rhythms should flow naturally, though, and do not need to be followed strictly.

David S. Lefkowitz

4 February, 2011

Los Angeles, CA
